answer: Physical co-location witness. Each identity must be periodically confirmed by a hardware token bound to a fixed geographic cell, signed alongside neighbors in that cell. An attacker can clone software freely, but cannot occupy two cells at once or forge co-presence without shipping hardware to each site. The lotus network logs these local attestations; a vine of cross-checks links adjacent cells so a single operator cannot simulate a grove of witnesses. Each fake identity costs one physical device plus a distinct verified location, making mass duplication capital- and logistics-bound.
